title: Number Complement
summary: Given an integer, return the integer obtained by flipping all its binary digits: 0's become 1's and 1's become 0's.
statement: Given an integer, return the integer obtained by flipping all its binary digits: 0's become 1's and 1's become 0's.
constraints: 0 <= num < 2^31. Flip only the significant bits, not an arbitrary fixed-width word; zero is represented by one digit, 0, and becomes 1.
Version 2 also covers Complement of Base 10 Integer (1009): source 476 requires num >= 1, while source 1009 additionally permits zero. Both source domains are supported.
Return the resulting nonnegative integer. Leading zero bits are not part of the input representation.
hints: Find the number of significant bits before flipping; zero still has one written digit.
Create an all-one mask of exactly that width, with a minimum width of one.
Compute width=max(1,num.bit_length()), mask=(1<<width)-1, and return mask XOR num.
A positive power of two becomes one less than itself; an all-one representation becomes zero. Zero itself becomes one.
editorial: XOR with a same-width all-one mask flips precisely the original bit positions. Python's bare ~ operator also changes infinitely many sign-extension bits, so it is not this contract. The independent oracle flips literal binary characters and parses the resulting string. Version 2 adds the zero input from source 1009 without changing any positive-input answer or progress ID.

tests.explanation: 1000 becomes 0111, giving 7; only these four positions are flipped.
